lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Synthesis and review: compound growth and volatility

objective: Learners synthesise compound and simple growth on the same invented amount and quantify the compounding advantage.
scenario: Yaminah is a made-up eighth grader modelling $6,000.00 over five simulated years at an invented 6% a year, once compounding annually and once as simple interest. All figures are invented.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Grow Yaminah's invented $6,000.00 at 6% a year for five years, compounding annually.

prompts.text: What is the compounded balance after five years?

tasks.directions: Compute five years of simple interest at the same rate on Yaminah's original amount, then the resulting balance.

prompts.text: What does one year of simple interest pay?
What is the simple-interest balance after five years?

tasks.directions: Quantify the compounding advantage for Yaminah and compare it with a single year of interest.

prompts.text: How much more does compounding produce over five years?
How much less is that five-year advantage than a single year of simple interest?

tasks.directions: Five years of compounding added less than one year of interest.

prompts.text: Explain why compounding looks unimpressive over Yaminah's five years, and what changes over twenty or thirty years.

remediation: If a learner multiplies the first year's interest by five for the compound case, write out each of Yaminah's years with its own opening balance.
extension: Ask the learner to project Yaminah's compounded balance for a tenth year and describe how the annual gain changes.
